introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0565 Human Biology 1, June 2020, Ordinary Level, Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board). Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; mark only one answer.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one best answer, A, B, C or D.

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the right pair of statement :
questions.corrige_markdown: Only one pair is a correct feature-and-function match. Opposable thumbs can be brought against the fingers, which lets a person grip and handle objects (C). Option A is too vague (a large forebrain gives intelligence, not simply living well in society). Option B is weak because being bipedal means walking on two feet, which makes balance harder, not more stable. In D, the head position is a result of upright posture, not the cause of it. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Man has a large developed forebrain... ...This enables man to live well in the society.
Man is bipedal.... This enables him to have a stable movement
Man has hands with opposable thumbs... ...This enables him to grip objects
Man's head is straight... This enables him to walk uprightly

questions.enonce_markdown: Which statement best defines a cell?
questions.corrige_markdown: A cell is the basic unit of life: it is both the unit of structure (organelles, membrane) and the unit of function (it carries out the life processes). Options A and C give only one of the two roles, and B does not say which kind of unit. Only D is complete. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Basic functional unit of an organism that can exist on its own
Basic unit of an organism that can exist on its own
Basic structural unit of an organism that can exist on its own
Basic structural and functional unit of an organism that can exist on its own

questions.enonce_markdown: How are the simple columnar epithelial cells modified to carry out their functions in the small intestines?
questions.corrige_markdown: The columnar cells lining the small intestine absorb digested food. Their free (lumen-facing) surface is folded into microvilli (a brush border), which greatly increases the surface area for absorption. Cilia (D) are found in the trachea and the oviduct, not in the small intestine. Being column shaped or elongated (A, B) describes the cell type, not a modification for absorption. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The cells are elongated in shape
The cells are column shaped and tightly fitted
The free borders of the cells have microvilli
The free borders of the cells have cilia

questions.enonce_markdown: In which part of the human body does meiosis take place?
questions.corrige_markdown: Meiosis makes the gametes (sperm and eggs). It takes place in the gonads: the testes in males and the ovaries in females. The bladder, a sense organ and the kidney contain only body cells, which divide by mitosis. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Two small pieces of bones were used to run an experiment. One was placed in dilute HCL and the other in water for same period of time, then removed. What could be the result?
questions.corrige_markdown: Bone is hard because of calcium salts (calcium phosphate and carbonate) deposited in a flexible collagen framework. Dilute hydrochloric acid dissolves the calcium salts, leaving the collagen, so the bone becomes soft and flexible (it can even be tied in a knot). The bone in water keeps its salts and stays hard. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: The bone in HCL was soft and flexible
The bone in water was a little bit soft
The bone in HCL was a bit hard

questions.enonce_markdown: Study the statements and select the best answer:
questions.corrige_markdown: Cardiac muscle is myogenic: it can start its own contractions without nerve impulses, which is why the heart beats rhythmically. Skeletal muscles contract and relax quickly (A is wrong), smooth muscles are involuntary (B is wrong), and bones are moved by skeletal muscles, not smooth muscles (D is wrong). **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Skeletal muscles contract and relax fairly slowly
Smooth muscles move bones at joints

questions.enonce_markdown: What type of joint is located at the elbow?
questions.corrige_markdown: The elbow allows movement in one plane only (bending and straightening the arm), like a door hinge. It is a hinge joint. Ball and socket joints are at the shoulder and hip. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the characteristics of a reflex action;
questions.corrige_markdown: A reflex action is inborn (innate), automatic (involuntary) and very fast because the impulse passes through a short pathway (receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone, motor neurone, effector) without needing a decision by the brain. A and D are wrong because a reflex is not learned, and B is wrong because it is not voluntary. Only C gives two correct characteristics. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagram below is the vertical section through the eye;

![fig-1](gce-ol-human-biology-2020-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

(Courtesy Bryon Dawson (Revised GCSE biology))

Identify the part that is concerned with colour vision
questions.corrige_markdown: Colour vision depends on the cone cells, which are found in the retina, the light-sensitive inner layer at the back of the eye. In the diagram, label i points to the lens region, ii to the ciliary body and suspensory ligaments region at the front, iii to the optic nerve leaving the eye, and iv to the retina at the back. So the part concerned with colour vision is IV. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the correct pair of ions which play a role in the transmission of impulse along the axon:
questions.corrige_markdown: A nerve impulse is an action potential. It is caused by sodium ions rushing into the axon (depolarisation) and potassium ions moving out (repolarisation) through channels in the axon membrane. Calcium ions act at the synapse, and magnesium ions play no direct role. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The flow diagram below is that of the control of blood sugar level. Study it and answer the question that follows:

![fig-2](gce-ol-human-biology-2020-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

(Courtesy Givens and Reiss Human biology and health studies)

Which activity is taking place at the corrective mechanism Y

*Options as printed:*
A) Liver converts glycogen to glucose
B) Liver converts glycogen to maltose
C) Insulin converts glucose to glycogen
D) Insulin accelerates conversion of glucose to glycogen
questions.corrige_markdown: The box Y is drawn in the middle of the cycle, between the two corrective mechanism boxes, so the figure does not say clearly which one is meant. If Y refers to the corrective mechanism after a rise above the norm (the upper one), the activity is that insulin, released by the pancreas, speeds up the conversion of glucose to glycogen in the liver (and muscles), which lowers the blood glucose level back to normal. This is best stated by option D, because insulin does not itself convert glucose: it stimulates the liver cells to do it, so C is less accurate. If Y referred to the lower mechanism (a fall below the norm), the activity would be glucagon making the liver convert glycogen to glucose (option A). Option B is wrong in both cases, since glycogen is broken down to glucose, not maltose. Because the position of Y is ambiguous and C and D are both close, no letter is designated. Most likely intended: D.

questions.enonce_markdown: The hormone whose release into blood causes an increase in heart beat is;
questions.corrige_markdown: Adrenaline, released by the adrenal glands in fear or excitement (fight or flight), speeds up the heart beat and raises blood pressure. Glucagon and insulin control blood sugar, and aldosterone controls sodium reabsorption in the kidney. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the vitamin that prevents night blindness:
questions.corrige_markdown: Vitamin A is needed to make rhodopsin, the pigment of the rod cells used for seeing in dim light. A lack of vitamin A causes night blindness. Vitamin B prevents beriberi, vitamin D prevents rickets and vitamin C prevents scurvy. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following activities will be affected if the bile duct is blocked ?
questions.corrige_markdown: Bile reaches the duodenum through the bile duct. It emulsifies fats into tiny droplets, giving lipase a larger surface to work on, and it neutralises the acid from the stomach. If the duct is blocked, fat digestion is reduced. Protein digestion and the secretion of pancreatic juice and secretin do not depend on bile. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Benedict's reagent is used to test for:
questions.corrige_markdown: Benedict's reagent is heated with the food sample: a colour change from blue to green, yellow, orange or brick-red shows a reducing sugar such as glucose. Starch is tested with iodine, proteins with biuret reagent and lipids with ethanol (emulsion test). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the mineral whose deficiency in the diet will result to goitre:
questions.corrige_markdown: Iodine is needed to make thyroxine in the thyroid gland. Without it the gland enlarges, a condition called goitre. Calcium deficiency causes rickets, and iron deficiency causes anaemia. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the component of the gastric juice that is bactericidal:
questions.corrige_markdown: Hydrochloric acid in gastric juice gives a pH of about 2, which kills most bacteria swallowed with food. It also activates pepsinogen. Mucus protects the stomach wall, pepsin digests proteins and rennin clots milk. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The maximum volume of air forced out after the deepest inspiration is called...
questions.corrige_markdown: Vital capacity is the largest volume of air that can be breathed out after a maximum inspiration (tidal volume + inspiratory reserve + expiratory reserve). The expiratory reserve volume is only the extra air breathed out after a normal breath out, and the residual volume stays in the lungs. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What activity brings about the expansion of the thorax during inspiration?
questions.corrige_markdown: During inspiration the diaphragm contracts and flattens, which increases the volume of the thorax from top to bottom. The external intercostal muscles also contract and move the ribs upwards and outwards. Relaxation (A, B) is what happens in expiration, and in D the ribs move outwards, not inwards, so D is wrong as printed. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Movement of ribs upwards and inwards

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study this table and select a difference between arteries and veins:

| | Arteries | Veins |
|---|---|---|
| A | Has valves | No valves |
| B | Large lumen | Small lumen |
| C | Thin elastic fibres | Thick elastic fibres |
| D | Thick muscular wall | Thin muscular wall |
questions.corrige_markdown: Arteries carry blood at high pressure, so their walls are thick, muscular and elastic with a narrow lumen. Veins carry blood at low pressure, so they have thin walls, a wide lumen and valves. Row A, B and C each state the opposite of the truth. Only row D is correct. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Why is high blood pressure the main factor that causes heart attack?
questions.corrige_markdown: With high blood pressure the heart must pump harder against the resistance in the arteries, so it works beyond its normal load. The cardiac muscle becomes overworked and may fail, leading to a heart attack. B is the opposite of what happens, and D is unrelated. A links to fatty deposits, but these are a cause of high blood pressure more than a result of it. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: It increases the risk of fatty deposits in the arteries
It causes less force to be exerted on the cardiac muscles
It causes the heart to work beyond normal
It increases the risk of high blood sugar level

questions.enonce_markdown: What will be the response of the skin during a vigorous activity?
questions.corrige_markdown: Vigorous activity produces extra heat. To cool the body, the arterioles in the skin dilate (vasodilation), more blood flows near the surface and much heat is lost by radiation, while sweating increases. Constriction, reduced sweating and closed pores (A, B, D) are responses to cold. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the part of the nephron where there is the highest reabsorption of salts:
questions.corrige_markdown: About 80 percent of the filtered salts (and all the glucose and amino acids) are reabsorbed in the proximal convoluted tubule, whose cells have microvilli and many mitochondria. The distal tubule and loop of Henle reabsorb smaller amounts, and the glomerulus only filters. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Laboratory analysis revealed the presence of glucose in the urine of an individual. What could be the disease he is suffering from?
questions.corrige_markdown: Normally all glucose is reabsorbed in the kidney. In diabetes mellitus the blood glucose is too high (insulin is lacking or ineffective), the kidney cannot reabsorb it all and glucose appears in the urine. The other diseases do not cause glucose in urine. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What type of immunity is acquired after exposure to a particular pathogen?
questions.corrige_markdown: When a person catches a disease naturally, their own body makes antibodies and memory cells: this is natural active immunity. Passive immunity means receiving ready-made antibodies (from the mother or by injection), and artificial immunity comes from vaccines or injections. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In the blood clotting mechanism fibrinogen changes to fibrin in the presence of:
questions.corrige_markdown: At a wound, the enzyme thrombin changes soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin threads, and calcium ions are needed in the clotting process. So the pair is thrombin and calcium ions. Prothrombin is the inactive precursor, and potassium ions are not involved in clotting. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the correct site and corresponding function of mucous membrane:

*Options as printed:*
A) In the gut.... Secretes mucus that coats food and prevents friction
B) In the vagina... Secretes mucus that prevents friction
C) In the nostrils... Secretes mucus that waft away dust and pathogens
D) In the mouth... Secretes mucus that traps pathogens
questions.corrige_markdown: Mucous membranes secrete mucus in many places. In the gut, mucus coats and lubricates food and protects the wall from enzymes (A is acceptable). In the vagina, mucus lubricates and protects (B is acceptable). In the nostrils, mucus traps dust and pathogens and the cilia then waft them away, so C is also acceptable although the sentence is badly worded. D (mouth) is the least precise. Because A, B and C are all defensible, no single letter can be designated. A likely intended key is C, the classic defence role of the nasal mucus.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Why are vaccines made of killed or attenuated pathogens?

*Options as printed:*
A) To prevent virulence of the pathogen
B) To prevent patients contracting the disease
C) To prevent allergic reactions from patients
D) To prevent resistance from patience
questions.corrige_markdown: A vaccine must make the body produce antibodies and memory cells without causing the disease. Killed or weakened (attenuated) pathogens cannot cause the disease, so they have lost their virulence (A). B is also defensible, since the vaccine must not give the patient the disease it is meant to prevent. C and D are wrong (D also contains the misprint 'patience'). Because A and B are both defensible, no letter is designated. Most likely intended: A.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which part of the female reproductive system produces oestrogen?
questions.corrige_markdown: Oestrogen is made by the follicle cells of the ovary (and progesterone by the corpus luteum). The clitoris, oviduct and uterus are target organs and do not produce it. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the hormone that induces labour in a pregnant mother?
questions.corrige_markdown: Oxytocin, released by the posterior pituitary gland, stimulates the uterine muscles to contract strongly at birth. Prolactin stimulates milk production, and progesterone maintains the pregnancy. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these birth control methods will prevent implantation?
questions.corrige_markdown: An intra-uterine device (IUD) is placed in the uterus. It stops a fertilised egg from implanting in the uterine wall. Contraceptive pills and hormonal implants mainly prevent ovulation, and tubal ligation blocks the oviducts so that the egg and sperm cannot meet. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: During which condition is the doctor authorized to carry out an abortion
questions.corrige_markdown: A doctor is authorised to carry out a medical abortion when continuing the pregnancy would endanger the mother's life or health. Not wanting the pregnancy, financial difficulty or the position of the baby are not medical grounds. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: When the mother's health cannot withstand the pregnancy
When the mother does not want the pregnancy
When the baby is lying upside down in the uterus
When the mother does not have enough financial means

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the diagram of the female reproductive system below :

![fig-3](gce-ol-human-biology-2020-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

(Courtesy D G Mackeans Introduction to human and social biology)

Identify the part where the egg develops during an ectopic pregnancy
questions.corrige_markdown: In an ectopic pregnancy the fertilised egg implants outside the uterus, most often in the oviduct (fallopian tube). In the diagram, i and ii point to the cervix and the uterus region, iii to the ovary end and iv to the oviduct. So the egg develops in the part labelled iv. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the part of the male reproductive system that produces the sperm cells:
questions.corrige_markdown: Sperm cells are made in the seminiferous tubules of the testes. The epididymis stores and matures them, and the sperm duct (vas deferens) carries them. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Choose the term that is applicable to the inheritance of the A B O blood groups:
questions.corrige_markdown: In the ABO system, alleles $I^A$ and $I^B$ are both expressed when present together, giving blood group AB. This is codominance (together with multiple alleles). Incomplete or partial dominance would give a blend, which does not happen. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The gene for albinism is recessive to the gene for skin colour. What are the possible genotypes of children born to a couple who are both heterozygous for the condition?
questions.corrige_markdown: Both parents are Aa. Gametes: A or a from each parent. Offspring: AA, Aa, Aa and aa, so the possible genotypes are AA, Aa and aa (ratio 1:2:1). Option A lists exactly these three. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Why is it rare to see characters of mutated genes in the society?
questions.corrige_markdown: Most mutant alleles are recessive, so they show in the phenotype only in homozygous individuals, which is rare. This is the underlying reason. B describes the effect (masking) rather than the cause. C is false (mutation is rare) and D is not an explanation. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Because most mutant genes are recessive
Because mutant genes are masked in the population
Because mutation is a common occurrence
Because mutation may result to new resistant species

questions.enonce_markdown: Why is the leaf dipped in alcohol to test for the presence of starch?
questions.corrige_markdown: After boiling the leaf in water to kill it, it is placed in hot ethanol (alcohol) to dissolve out the green chlorophyll. The leaf becomes pale so that the blue-black colour of starch with iodine can be seen clearly. The boiling water softens the leaf and kills the cells. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What percentage of energy is transferred from one level to the next level in a food chain?
questions.corrige_markdown: Only about 10 percent of the energy at one trophic level passes to the next. The rest is lost as heat in respiration, in waste, and in parts not eaten. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the best first aid treatment you would give to an individual with minor burns?
questions.corrige_markdown: For a minor burn the first treatment is to cool the burn with cold running water, which reduces the heat, pain and damage to the skin. Salt would hurt the skin, a cloth alone does not cool the burn, and a minor burn does not need an ambulance. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Pour abundant salt on affected area
Flood affected area with cold water
Cover affected area with clean cloth

questions.enonce_markdown: How would you prevent the walls of the house from being overheated by direct sun rays?
questions.corrige_markdown: Extended eaves (the overhanging edge of the roof) throw shade on the walls, so the sun's rays do not fall directly on them. Air vents and ventilation bricks let air circulate but do not shade the walls, and gutters only carry rain water. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
What is the advantage of the biological filter method over the activated sludge method in the treatment of sewage?

*Options as printed:*
A) It is faster
B) It is less tedious
C) It produces more useful products
D) It is cheaper
questions.corrige_markdown: In the biological (trickling) filter, sewage is sprayed over a bed of stones covered with microbes, which needs little energy and little supervision. The activated sludge method needs constant aeration and monitoring, so it is faster but more costly and demanding. Both B (less tedious) and D (cheaper) are therefore defensible advantages of the filter, while A is false (activated sludge is faster) and C is not a distinguishing advantage. No letter is designated. Most likely intended: D.

questions.enonce_markdown: By what process does water vapour from the atmosphere become cloud
questions.corrige_markdown: Water vapour rising into the cold upper air cools and changes to tiny liquid droplets, which form clouds. This change from gas to liquid is condensation. Evaporation is the reverse, precipitation is rain or snow falling, and guttation is loss of water drops from leaves. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The water pollutant that causes algal bloom is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Raw sewage (like fertiliser run-off) is rich in nitrates and phosphates, which make algae grow explosively (algal bloom) and lead to eutrophication. Sulphur dioxide and acid rain are air pollutants that acidify water, and radioactive material does not feed algae. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: One way to take care of the ear is by:
questions.corrige_markdown: Loud sounds can damage the sensory cells of the cochlea and cause deafness, so staying away from high sounds protects hearing. Cotton buds push wax in and can injure the eardrum, rest does not protect the ear, and washing inside the ear can push in water and dirt. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Using clean cotton buds to remove wax from the ear
Wash ears regularly to keep it clean

questions.enonce_markdown: To which health unit would you take an individual who has just been involved in a car accident
questions.corrige_markdown: A person who has just had an accident needs immediate care, which is given by the emergency (casualty) unit. Surgery and admission to a ward may follow after assessment. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the biological significance of storing food in a cold place?
questions.corrige_markdown: Low temperature slows down the enzymes of bacteria and fungi, so they cannot grow and multiply, and the food does not spoil. Cold storage does not keep vermin away and its main significance is not taste. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select a role of a public health inspector:
questions.corrige_markdown: A public health inspector checks that buildings, markets, food premises and sanitation meet hygiene standards and advises people. Punishing, demolition and training veterinarians are not their roles. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Punishes vendors with dirty business premises
Ensures that construction meets hygiene standards
Destroys houses that are haphazardly constructed
Educate vet doctors on meat inspection

questions.enonce_markdown: The process of converting nitrate to nitrogen gas found in the atmosphere.
questions.corrige_markdown: Denitrifying bacteria, in waterlogged soil with little oxygen, change nitrates into nitrogen gas, which returns to the atmosphere. Nitrogen fixation does the opposite (nitrogen gas to nitrogen compounds), ammonification makes ammonia from dead matter, and eutrophication is enrichment of water. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the disease that can be spread through exchange of towels.
questions.corrige_markdown: Ringworm is a fungal skin infection spread by direct contact and by sharing towels, combs and clothes. AIDS is spread through body fluids, and dysentery and cholera are spread by contaminated food and water. **Answer: B.**
